faqs.question: When exactly is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 8 February 2027. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and Valentine's Day closes the week on Sunday 14 February. In 2026 Propose Day fell on a Sunday, so a plan reused from last year assumes a clear weekend day you will not have.

faqs.question: Is it safe to just translate a Hindi propose day quote into Marathi?
faqs.answer: No, and it is the failure a Marathi reader catches fastest. Hindi and Marathi share Devanagari but not grammar: the copula is आहे / आहेस / आहोत rather than है / हो / हैं, the dative is मला and तुला rather than मुझे and तुम्हें, and Marathi has no तुम at all.

faqs.question: Should I say तू or तुम्ही when I propose in Marathi?
faqs.answer: तू for someone you are already close to, तुम्ही for a first meeting, an arranged introduction, or anyone you address respectfully. Marathi has no middle option the way Hindi's तुम is a middle option, so the choice is a real one and it changes the verb ending too.

faqs.question: How do I actually say I love you in Marathi?
faqs.answer: मी तुझ्यावर प्रेम करतो if you are a man, मी तुझ्यावर प्रेम करते if you are a woman. Note प्रेम, not प्यार — प्यार is Hindi and reads as Hindi even in Devanagari.

faqs.question: What is the Marathi line for will you marry me?
faqs.answer: माझ्यासोबत आयुष्यभर चालशील का? is the warm version — "will you walk with me for a lifetime". The word for marriage itself is लग्न, not शादी, which is one of the quickest tells that a line was written in Marathi rather than converted from Hindi.

faqs.question: Why do some of these lines change depending on whether I am a man or a woman?
faqs.answer: Marathi marks the speaker's gender inside the verb in the present and past tense. A man says करतो, सांगतोय, बघतो, गोंधळलो, कंटाळलो; a woman says करते, सांगतेय, बघते, गोंधळले, कंटाळले. Both forms are given on the page wherever the switch matters.

faqs.question: Do I need a Marathi keyboard to send these?
faqs.answer: No. You can copy the Devanagari line straight from this page and paste it into WhatsApp, Instagram or a SubhSandesh page field. If you want to type it yourself, both Android and iOS ship a Marathi keyboard you can add in settings.

faqs.question: Can I build a SubhSandesh page that is entirely in Marathi?
faqs.answer: Not today. You can type, paste and display Marathi in Devanagari inside the fields you fill in — your line, the names, the captions — but the interface, the buttons and the built-in copy are English, and there is no Marathi UI to switch to.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Quotes in Marathi for Monday 8 February 2027

Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday 8 February**, the second day of Valentine week — Rose Day opens it on Sunday 7 February, Valentine's Day closes it on Sunday 14 February. Below are 19 propose day quotes in Marathi, in Devanagari, each with a Roman transliteration and an English meaning, grouped by who you are asking. The delivery numbers here are SubhSandesh's own, platform-wide across all 16 page types: 4,567 personalised pages built since 12 March 2026, 92.7% of them published and shared (4,234 of 4,567), and 48.9% of views landing on a phone (25,167 of 51,504). Check the weekday before planning — Propose Day 2026 fell on a Sunday, so last year's plan assumes a clear weekend day that 2027 does not give you.

## Why Marathi and "Hindi in Devanagari" are not the same thing

Marathi and Hindi share a script, not a grammar. The Marathi copula runs आहे / आहेस / आहोत where Hindi runs है / हो / हैं; the dative is मला and तुला, not मुझे and तुम्हें; and there is no तुम at all — the second person is तू or तुम्ही, with nothing between.

Vocabulary splits too: प्रेम not प्यार, आयुष्य not ज़िंदगी, नाव not नाम, गोष्ट not बात, हो not हाँ, लग्न not शादी. A Marathi reader spots a Hindi sentence in Devanagari in the time it takes to read it, and that is the one mistake you cannot walk back on 8 February.

The sharpest test is आवडणे. "I like you" is मला तू आवडतेस — literally "you are liked to me" — and no Hindi sentence has that shape. Every line below carries at least one construction of that kind and was screened against a blocklist of Hindi-only forms.

## 19 propose day quotes in Marathi, grouped by who you are asking

Gender changes the line from the inside. A man says करतो, सांगतोय, बघतो, गोंधळलो, कंटाळलो; a woman says करते, सांगतेय, बघते, गोंधळले, कंटाळले. Addressed to a woman a line ends आवडतेस or हवी आहेस; to a man, आवडतोस or हवा आहेस. Thirteen further lines were written and dropped: two leaned on film-song phrasing, three used imagery that could not be verified as natural Marathi rather than translated Hindi, one hinged on the ambiguous आपण, and seven went for length.

### 1. For a first ask, in the तू register

**तुझ्या डोळ्यांत बघितलं की माझं बोलणंच थांबतं — आज मात्र मी बोलणार आहे.**
*tujhyā ḍoḷyānt baghitlaṁ kī mājhaṁ bolṇaṁch thāmbtaṁ — āj mātra mī bolṇār āhe.*
Your eyes stop my words. Today, though, I am going to speak.

**मी खूप काही मागत नाही — फक्त तुझी सोबत, रोजच्या रोज.**
*mī khūp kāhī māgat nāhī — phakta tujhī sobat, rojchyā roj.*
I am not asking for much — only your company, day after day.

**तुझ्यासोबत घालवलेला प्रत्येक क्षण मला पुन्हा जगावासा वाटतो.**
*tujhyāsobat ghālavlelā pratyek kṣaṇ malā punhā jagāvāsā vāṭto.*
Every moment spent with you makes me want to live it again.

**मला तुझ्यापासून काहीच लपवायचं नाही — म्हणून हे आधी सांगतोय: मी तुझ्यावर प्रेम करतो.**
*malā tujhyāpāsūn kāhīch lapvāyachaṁ nāhī — mhaṇūn he ādhī sāngtoy: mī tujhyāvar prem karto.*
I want to hide nothing from you, so this first: I love you.

### 2. For a marriage proposal, where the word is लग्न

**माझ्यासोबत आयुष्यभर चालशील का? बाकी सगळं आपण वाटून घेऊ.**
*mājhyāsobat āyuṣyabhar chālśīl kā? bākī sagḷaṁ āpaṇ vāṭūn gheū.*
Will you walk with me for a lifetime? The rest we divide between us.

**मला थाटामाटाचं लग्न नको आहे, मला फक्त तू हवी आहेस.**
*malā thāṭāmāṭāchaṁ lagna nako āhe, malā phakta tū havī āhes.*
I do not want a grand wedding. I only want you.

**तुझ्या नावापुढे माझं नाव लावायची परवानगी मागतोय.**
*tujhyā nāvāpuḍhe mājhaṁ nāv lāvāyachī paravāngī māgtoy.*
I am asking permission to put my name after yours.

**लग्न म्हणजे मोठा निर्णय — पण तुझ्याबाबतीत मी कधीच गोंधळलो नाही.**
*lagna mhaṇje moṭhā nirṇay — paṇ tujhyābābtīt mī kadhīch gondhaḷlo nāhī.*
Marriage is a big decision. About you I was never once in doubt.

**आपण दोघं मिळून एक घर उभं करू — त्या घराचं पहिलं वाक्य तूच असशील.**
*āpaṇ doghaṁ miḷūn ek ghar ubhaṁ karū — tyā gharāchaṁ pahilaṁ vākya tūch asśīl.*
We two will build a home, and you will be its first sentence.

### 3. For a partner you have already been with for years

**इतकी वर्षं झाली, तरी तुझं नाव ऐकलं की अजूनही छातीत काहीतरी हलतं.**
*itkī varṣaṁ jhālī, tarī tujhaṁ nāv aikalṁ kī ajūnhī chhātīt kāhītarī haltaṁ.*
All these years, and your name still moves something in my chest.

**तुझ्या सवयी मला पाठ आहेत, आणि तरीही मी कंटाळलो नाही — हेच माझं उत्तर आहे.**
*tujhyā savayī malā pāṭh āhet, āṇi tarīhī mī kaṇṭāḷlo nāhī — hech mājhaṁ uttar āhe.*
I know your habits by heart and am still not bored. That is my answer.

**भांडणं होतील, रुसवे होतील — पण मी हात सोडणार नाही.**
*bhāṇḍaṇaṁ hotīl, rusve hotīl — paṇ mī hāt soḍṇār nāhī.*
There will be quarrels and sulks. I am not letting go of your hand.

### 4. For someone you have not told yet

**हे सांगायला मला खूप वेळ लागला. आता ऐक: मला तू आवडतेस.**
*he sāngāyalā malā khūp veḷ lāgalā. ātā aik: malā tū āvaḍtes.*
This took me a long time to say. Now listen: I like you.

**मी घाबरत घाबरत विचारतोय, पण विचारल्याशिवाय राहवत नाही.**
*mī ghābrat ghābrat vichārtoy, paṇ vichāralyāśivāy rāhvat nāhī.*
I am asking nervously, but I cannot bear to leave it unasked.

### 5. For the तुम्ही register — formal, respectful, or a first meeting

**तुम्ही होकार दिलात, तर पुढचं सगळं आयुष्य मी तुमच्या सोबतीने ठरवेन.**
*tumhī hokār dilāt, tar puḍhchaṁ sagḷaṁ āyuṣya mī tumchyā sobatīne ṭharaven.*
If you say yes, I will plan the rest of my life alongside you.

**माझं म्हणणं थोडक्यात — मला तुमच्याबरोबर संसार करायचा आहे.**
*mājhaṁ mhaṇṇaṁ thoḍakyāt — malā tumchyābarobar saṁsār karāyachā āhe.*
My case, in short: I want to make a life with you.

### 6. Short lines for a card, a status or a page's last screen

**तू म्हणजे माझा सगळ्यात सोपा निर्णय.**
*tū mhaṇje mājhā sagḷyāt sopā nirṇay.*
You are my easiest decision.

**होकार दे. बाकीचं मी बघतो.**
*hokār de. bākīchaṁ mī baghto.*
Say yes. I will handle the rest.

**तुझ्यावाचून मला करमत नाही.**
*tujhyāvāchūn malā karmat nāhī.*
Nothing passes agreeably without you. करमणे has no one-word Hindi equivalent.

## Where a Marathi line actually lands, and who else reads it

All four routes take Devanagari; they differ in audience. The first-party column is platform-wide across all 16 page types — there is no proposal-specific figure, because a read-only probe of the proposal pages collection was refused.

| Where the line goes | Devanagari support | Who can read it | SubhSandesh first-party signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp or SMS | Native on Android and iOS | One person | Not measured — outside SubhSandesh |
| Instagram story | Native, but the app picks the font | Every follower | Not measured — outside SubhSandesh |
| A SubhSandesh page you share | You paste the Devanagari in | Anyone with the link | 48.9% of views are on a phone (25,167 of 51,504), platform-wide |
| A SubhSandesh page you lock | Same | Only who gets the password | 39.9% of creators lock before sharing (1,822 of 4,567), platform-wide |

The choice is about audience, not typography. If you would not want a follower list reading the line, the locked page is the only one of the four giving you that control — and the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is the page built for the ask itself, ending on a YES button that grows every time they dodge it. Budget real time: the median gap from first save to last edit is 6.4 hours, sampled on the "I love you" page (/love-gf), n=1,138.

## When /proposal is the wrong page for your Propose Day line

Most Propose Day traffic is not a marriage proposal, and /proposal is built for "will you marry me" specifically. If you mean "will you be my girlfriend", the [romantic 'I love you' page](/love-gf) is the honest fit — the most-built page on the platform at 1,138 pages, 24.9% of everything created, and the most-viewed at 16,362 views, 31.8% of all views. If you are asking someone out rather than proposing, [The Invitation](/date-invitation) fits better: a yes there becomes a countdown, not a commitment.

The second limit matters more here. **The templates are English-language.** You can type, paste and display Marathi in Devanagari in the fields you fill — your line, the names, the captions — but the interface, the buttons and the built-in copy are English, and there is no Marathi UI. If you want every word including the chrome in Marathi, SubhSandesh cannot give you that today, and a plain WhatsApp message serves you better.

## Why good Marathi writing is scarce online in the first place

The supply gap is documented, not anecdotal. The 2022 paper introducing [L3Cube-MahaCorpus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01159), a Marathi corpus of 24.8 million sentences and 289 million tokens scraped from internet sources, states plainly that "Marathi is a popular language in India but still lacks these resources".

That is not a Marathi-only problem, but Marathi is squarely inside it. The [Internet Policy Review entry on digitally-disadvantaged languages](https://policyreview.info/glossary/digitally-disadvantaged-languages) (11 April 2022) names Marathi among the languages written in Devanagari and cites Kornai's estimate that at most 5% of the world's 7,000-plus languages will reach "digital vitality".

Demand runs the other way. The KPMG–Google study [Indian Languages — Defining India's Internet](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/in/pdf/2017/04/Indian-languages-Defining-Indias-Internet.pdf) (April 2017) counted 89 million primary Marathi speakers in India in 2016, and an Indian-language internet user base of 234 million at the end of that year — up at a 41% compound rate since 2011, already larger than the English-language base. A large audience, a thin shelf.

The thinness is recent, not inherent: Pär Eliasson's 2025 survey of [early modern missionary dictionaries of Konkani and Marathi](https://journals.uu.se/orientaliasuecana/article/view/654) records Marathi dictionaries compiled in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries — four centuries of separate lexicography, for a language a generative tool will still hand you in Hindi.

failed.why: The slug keeps the stop word "in" because it is the exact assigned target keyword (propose day quotes in marathi); dropping it would break the keyword-in-slug match the same checklist demands.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Target position 6-10, not 3. This SERP is a February news cycle owned by Loksatta, Times Now, Maharashtra Times and Zee, whose domain authority is far above ours and who refresh these pages every year; the realistic edge is freshness and correctness - they are still ranking with 2025 in their titles, and none of them prints that Propose Day 2027 is a Monday or tells a reader which of their lines is actually Hindi in Devanagari. An answer engine has a reason to cite this for the date, the Marathi-versus-Hindi test and the transliterations; it has no reason to cite it for authority, and ranking will take months if it happens at all.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific SubhSandesh data exists: a read-only probe of the proposalpages collection was refused by this machine's production-read policy, in wave 1 and again here. Every figure in this post is therefore labelled in the body prose as platform-wide across all 16 page types, or as sampled on /love-gf (n=1,138). No number is attributed to proposal pages.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty, so the post states and implies no price, no free tier and no paid tier anywhere.

Phase 1 could not be run as specified: this session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted before the keyword could be searched, so no competitor page was fetched. The SERP shape used here is the one measured directly on 2026-09-16 and supplied in the assignment - Loksatta, Times Now, Maharashtra Times and Zee, with Loksatta and Times Now still carrying 2025 in their titles. The 'at least one claim none of the top 5 pages make' item is passed on that evidence (the verified 2027 weekday, the Hindi-in-Devanagari screen, the published cut count) rather than on a page-by-page read.

Marathi line verification is editorial, not external: each published line was screened for at least one Marathi-only construction (the आहे/आहेस/आहोत copula, dative मला/तुला, the -तोय/-तेय progressive, आवडणे, करमणे, संसार करणे, sentence-final का) and against a programmatic blocklist of Hindi-only forms (मैं, तुम, हूँ, है, क्या, प्यार, दिल, ज़िंदगी, हमेशा, बहुत, बात, शादी, मुझे, तुम्हें). Thirteen drafted lines were cut rather than published unverified. No native-speaker review was available in this run.

The Orientalia Suecana citation rests on the article's abstract page only; the full PDF was not read. The KPMG-Google PDF was read in full via text extraction, and the L3Cube and Internet Policy Review claims come from pages read in full.

Four sources rather than five: a fifth (Joshi et al., ACL 2020, on language-resource disparity) was drafted, verified and then removed because aclanthology.org and arxiv.org had each reached the batch's 3-post domain cap while 29 siblings were still writing. The remaining four satisfy the subject, peer-review and open-access requirements without holding two capped domains.
